newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Howard launches environment plan.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Howard launches environment plan.

text.p: The Australian government launched a A$1.25 billion (US$975 million) fund on Thursday to fulfil a pledge to repair and protect the environment.

The Natural Heritage Trust Fund's main target will be to clean up the basin of the Murray and Darling rivers, which produces half Australia's valuable farm output but has been hit by salinity, land degradation and other problems.

"The trust will deliver a better environment for all... cleaner beaches, less air pollution, healthier rivers and waterways, more productive land and increased protection for our unique wildlife," Environment Minister Robert Hill said in a statement.
The Liberal-National coalition proposed the fund in the March 1996 election campaign in a bid to lure the powerful green vote away from its traditional support for the then Labor government.
The five-year fund will be paid for by the partial sale of telecoms giant Telstra Corp, to be sold off later this year.

The fund will pay for a range of other programmes, including cleaning up coastal waters and protecting wildlife. Prime Minister John Howard announced the first A$6 million (US$4.5 million) worth of funds on Thursday, mostly targeted at the Murray-Darling basin.
The basin is a diverse ecosystem of alps, deserts and 30,000 wetlands stretching through eastern Australia from Queensland state in the north to South Australia.
The government has budgeted more than A$160 million for the fund in the fiscal year from July.
But Greens Party parliamentarian Bob Brown said the heritage fund would simply repair damage that resulted from flawed government policies in other areas.
Brown said the fund would help combat salinity downstream in the Murray-Darling basin while other policies exacerbated the problem by allowing rapid forest clearing upstream.

"I think a lot of this money -- the big ticket items -- in the Natural Heritage Trust fund are going to be seen to be chasing environmental repair in an area where the government's policies are actually leading to environmental despair," he said.
